definitions.UTC: Coordinated Universal Time. Civil atomic time scale broadcast by standard frequency stations. Ticks at the SI second rate of TAI, with integer leap seconds inserted periodically to maintain |UTC - UT1| < 0.9s. Modern UTC definition instituted on 1972-01-01.
definitions.UT1: Universal Time 1. Non-uniform astronomical time scale tied strictly to the diurnal rotation of the Earth relative to the Celestial Intermediate Origin (CIO). Subject to tidal deceleration and atmospheric/core irregularities.
definitions.TAI: International Atomic Time. Continuous statistical atomic time scale calculated by the BIPM from primary cesium frequency standards. No leap seconds.
definitions.TT: Terrestrial Time. Theoretical uniform dynamical time scale for geocentric ephemerides, representing proper time on the rotating geoid. Fixed by IAU definition as TT = TAI + 32.184s.
definitions.TDB: Barycentric Dynamical Time. Relativistic coordinate time scale for the Solar System Barycenter (SSB). Evaluated on Earth, TDB differs from TT by small periodic relativistic terms: |TDB - TT| < 1.66 ms.
definitions.DeltaT_astronomical: Astronomical Delta-T defined as Delta-T = TT - UT1 (or historically ET - UT). Quantifies cumulative Earth rotational deceleration against uniform dynamical time.
definitions.TT_minus_UTC: The discrete offset between Terrestrial Time and civil atomic UTC for dates >= 1972-01-01: TT - UTC = (TAI - UTC) + 32.184s = Delta_AT + 32.184s.
definitions.DUT1: DUT1 = UT1 - UTC. Maintained within [-0.9s, +0.9s] by the IERS via leap-second insertions.

j2000Investigation.forensicResolution: The Phase 4F.6B statement that J2000.0 Delta-T is exactly 64.184s is mathematically true ONLY for TT - UTC (32s + 32.184s). Astronomical Delta-T (TT - UT1) at J2000.0 was approximately 63.83s (differing by DUT1 = +0.355s). The production ephemeris code converting UTC calendar input to TT needs TT - UTC (64.184s), which matches the exact physical quantity returned by getDeltaT for modern dates.

functions.name: getDeltaT
functions.purpose: Calculates the offset in seconds required to convert a civil Julian Day to dynamical Terrestrial Time (TT).
functions.inputScale: Civil Julian Day: UTC for dates >= 1972-01-01; UT1 / GMT for dates < 1972-01-01.
functions.outputScale: Seconds to add to civil time. Returns TT - UTC for modern dates (>= 1972); returns Delta-T = TT - UT1 for historical dates (< 1972).

conversionFormula.modern: For jd >= 2441317.5: (TAI - UTC) + 32.184s from IERS leap-second table.
conversionFormula.historical: For jd < 2441317.5: Piecewise polynomials of Fred Espenak & Jean Meeus (NASA TP-2006-214141) covering 11 historical intervals.

functions.applicableEpochRange: Ancient eras (-3000 BCE) to foreseeable future (2100+ CE).
assumptions: Modern era assumes standard IERS Bulletin C leap-second table.
Future dates (> 2017) hold the offset constant at 69.184s, matching NASA JPL Horizons operational policy.
Historical dates assume civil records reflect Greenwich Mean Time / UT1.

uncertainty.future: Accumulates ~1-2s per decade of unannounced future leap seconds

functions.invalidInputHandling: Returns 0 safely for NaN, non-number, null, or non-finite inputs.

functions.name: utcToTT
functions.purpose: Converts a Julian Day Number in civil time (UTC / UT1) to dynamical Terrestrial Time (TT / TDB).
functions.inputScale: Julian Day Number in UTC (for jd >= 2441317.5) or UT1 (for jd < 2441317.5).
functions.outputScale: Julian Day Number in Terrestrial Time (TT).
functions.assumptions: TDB is approximated by TT (difference |TDB - TT| < 1.66 ms, corresponding to < 0.000003 arcseconds in Saturn longitude).
functions.uncertainty: Inherited directly from getDeltaT uncertainty divided by 86400 days.
functions.invalidInputHandling: Returns NaN safely for NaN, non-number, null, undefined, or non-finite inputs.

functions.name: ttToUTC
functions.purpose: Converts a Julian Day Number in Terrestrial Time (TT) back to civil time (UTC / UT1).
functions.inputScale: Julian Day Number in Terrestrial Time (TT).
functions.outputScale: Julian Day Number in civil time (UTC for jd >= 2441317.5; UT1 for jd < 2441317.5).
functions.applicableEpochRange: All continuous intervals outside instantaneous leap-second boundary steps.
functions.assumptions: Assumes getDeltaT(jdTT) ≈ getDeltaT(jdUtc), which holds within 0.1 ms on continuous domains because d(DeltaT)/dt < 1.0 s/year.
functions.invalidInputHandling: Returns NaN safely for NaN, non-number, null, undefined, or non-finite inputs.

functions.name: dateToJD
functions.signature: dateToJD(year, month, day, hour = 0, min = 0, sec = 0): number
functions.purpose: Converts Gregorian calendar date and time components into a continuous Julian Day Number.
functions.inputScale: Calendar components in any uniform or civil time scale (UTC, UT1, or Local Civil).
functions.outputScale: Julian Day Number in the exact same time scale as the input components.
functions.conversionFormula: decimalDay = day + (hour + min / 60 + sec / 3600) / 24; standard Meeus astronomical algorithm with Gregorian leap year rule.
functions.applicableEpochRange: Gregorian calendar dates (-4712 BCE to 4000+ CE).
functions.assumptions: Does not perform time-scale conversion; output time scale is identical to input time scale.
functions.uncertainty: Mathematically exact to floating-point precision (~1e-11 days).
functions.invalidInputHandling: Produces NaN if non-numerical arguments are provided.

functions.name: generateKundali
functions.signature: generateKundali(birthDate, birthTime, latitude, longitude, timezone, ayanamsaSystem = 'LAHIRI'): object
functions.purpose: Primary user-facing astrology chart generation function converting user birth inputs to astronomical and astrological positions.
functions.inputScale: Local Civil Timestamp with explicit numerical timezone offset (hours east of Greenwich, e.g. +5.5 for IST).
functions.outputScale: Kundali chart object containing planetary sidereal longitudes, house cusps, ascendant, and Julian Day in UTC/GMT.
functions.conversionFormula: utcHour = hour - timezone; jd = dateToJD(year, month, day, utcHour, minute, 0); saturnLongitude evaluates utcToTT(jd).
assumptions: User supplies local standard clock time and the applicable timezone offset.
Subtracting timezone converts local civil time to Greenwich civil time (UTC for >= 1972; GMT/UT1 for < 1972).
A Delta-T polynomial does NOT convert local time to UT1; timezone subtraction performs local-to-Greenwich conversion.
functions.uncertainty: Subject to user-provided timezone accuracy; historical dates before standard time zones (e.g. pre-1906 in India) require Local Mean Time (LMT = lon / 15.0).
functions.invalidInputHandling: If timezone is missing or undefined, utcHour evaluates to NaN, resulting in safe NaN propagation in calculations.
